investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. As a result the pod remained Unschedulable for ~131–150 s across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received an empty evidence object, failing every required-evidence assertion in the contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. As a result the pod remained Unschedulable for ~131–150 s across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received an empty evidence object, failing every required-evidence assertion in the contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm runtime in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes (peer-pod VM slots), and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~131–148 s), preventing the eval from reaching the agent runtime and producing any evidence. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is scoped to the eval environment's Kubernetes cluster. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by other workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning even if VM slots were freed on those nodes they could not be used. This could be a pre-existing constraint or a recent node label change not reflected in the evidence.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval runs: all three checks ran sequentially within ~5 minutes (05:28–05:33 UTC) and each consumed a VM slot attempt; if prior runs or other workloads did not release slots, the pool may have been depleted before this run began.

LOW — transient scheduler state: a brief scheduler backlog or node NotReady condition could produce a temporary Unschedulable result, but the identical error across three independent checks over 5 minutes makes a transient cause less likely.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of any remote-agent check that produces a scheduled pod and returns evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) would disprove that the cluster is currently capacity-constrained.

kubectl output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable > requested on the 2 eligible nodes would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause and point instead to a scheduler policy or affinity misconfiguration.
Evidence that the 4 non-matching nodes recently had their labels changed or removed (making them newly ineligible) would shift the primary cause from VM slot exhaustion to affinity/selector drift.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state at the same time as this failure would disprove the shared-capacity hypothesis and suggest the failure is isolated to the runtime check's pod spec.
Logs showing the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs successfully terminated all prior eval pods would disprove the pod-leak hypothesis.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the expected number of nodes (e.g., at least 2) match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules, alerting on node label drift before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes between 'pod scheduled but runtime slow' and 'pod never scheduled' failure modes, enabling faster triage by surfacing the scheduling error as a distinct check status rather than a generic timeout.
